title: A lookup (a join): each record reads the row of a second file that has its key
proves: <variable source="*.ent.csv" storage="data"> holds every row of a second file, and a script selects the row with the key of the current record
a key with no row in the second file gives None, and the script writes a default (UNKNOWN)
several records read the same row, and the first and the last row of the second file are found
an empty column of the found row stays empty text, and the script can replace it
the lookup variables and an unlisted source column are not output fields
a list comprehension spells the same lookup, and the order of the second file does not change the result
the lookup table in a <nestedKey> is an output field, a key of another type finds no row, a missing default fails the run, and <variable> has no where=
a script can use the builtins that scripts offer (str), and open() and next() fail with I957, which names the builtin; a bare builtin name that is no field (id) stays I832
where= reads only the current file row: a where= that reads parent. fails with I832 and the where= guidance
the lookup variable goes inside the <generate> (a setup-level one fails with I830); a where= value error gets the issue resolution, not the scope hint; a key script name failure keeps the scope hint

patch.old: script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}.get(branch_id)"
patch.new: script="([b for b in branches if b.branch_id == branch_id] or [None])[0]"

patch.old:
<variable name="branches" source="data/entity/branches.ent.csv" storage="data" distribution="ordered"/>
        <variable name="branch" script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}
patch.new:
<nestedKey name="branches" type="list" source="data/entity/branches.ent.csv" distribution="ordered"/>
        <variable name="branch" script="{b.branch_id: b for b in this.branches}

negatives.name: a_variable_has_no_where
negatives.remediation: where= keeps rows of a <generate> or <iterate> file source. To look up a row of another file

patch.old: <variable name="branch" script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}.get(branch_id)"/>

negatives.name: a_script_cannot_open_a_file
negatives.run_error: calls the Python builtin 'open', which scripts do not offer
negatives.remediation: Scripts offer these Python builtins: abs, all, any, bin

negatives.name: next_is_no_script_builtin
negatives.run_error: calls the Python builtin 'next', which scripts do not offer
negatives.remediation: Write next(...) as ([x for x in rows if ...] or [None])[0]

patch.old: script="{b.branch_id: b for b in branches}.get(branch_id)"
patch.new: script="next((b for b in branches if b.branch_id == branch_id), None)"

negatives.name: a_bare_builtin_name_is_a_missing_field
negatives.run_error: NameError: name 'id' is not defined: check spelling
negatives.remediation: Use parent.name for the immediate enclosing scope

negatives.name: where_reads_only_the_current_row
negatives.run_error: where= reads only the current file row
negatives.remediation: where= reads only the current file row: its columns bare or as this.<column>, and the expression functions; parent., root., a <variable> and a setup name do not exist there. Every column is text: cast it

patch.old:
<generate name="account_view" source="data/entity/accounts.ent.csv" distribution="ordered" columns="account_id, branch_id">
        <!-- storage="data" holds every row of the file, the same list in each record; a variable is no output field.
             branch is None when no branch row has the key. Both keys are file text. -->
        <variable name="branches" source="data/entity/branches.ent.csv" storage="data" distribution="ordered"/>
patch.new:
<variable name="branches" source="data/entity/branches.ent.csv" storage="data" distribution="ordered"/>
    <generate name="account_view" source="data/entity/accounts.ent.csv" distribution="ordered" columns="account_id, branch_id">
        <!-- storage="data" holds every row of the file, the same list in each record; a variable is no output field.
             branch is None when no branch row has the key. Both keys are file text. -->
